rows.explainer: **Changed for consistency.** Ambitious Impact discounts the costs of reaching households at its fixed cost rate (4%), while the impacts of reaching them fade with the chance the change happens anyway (5% a year) and grow with the population (2%). rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: Units of value per dollar
rows.explainer: Ambitious Impact counts income in years of doubled consumption. A doubling for a year is ln 2 of log-consumption, which is one GiveWell unit of value at the shared value of income, so the result ranks with the GiveWell models. With credit by share of resources, times the share of the full cost paid in cash (staff's forgone pay is the rest).

summary: Ambitious Impact's estimate (2026 idea report) for a new charity helping smallholder farmers in Kenya get low-risk loans secured on the asset they buy, such as a water tank. The idea Better Season Project was founded to run. Its bottom line is the cost per year of doubled household consumption, including the chance the charity fails.

theoretical.reason: Ambitious Impact's estimate of the idea, written before the charity existed; not based on the charity's own results.
theoretical.runs: Better Season Project partners with Kenyan savings cooperatives to lend smallholders money for rainwater tanks secured on the tank (piloting).
